children: NeGD to act as Knowledge Partner; CISF personnel to train at Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), Defence Institute of Advanced Technology (DIAT), DRDO) laboratories and other Centres of Excellence

New Delhi, October 24: The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the National e-Governance Division (NeGD), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), for structured training of its personnel in emerging technologies.
The partnership comes at a time when drones, artificial intelligence and cyber tools are changing the nature of threats to the country's critical infrastructure.

CISF protects airports, nuclear power plants, metro systems, ports and other critical infrastructure and strategic installations, which now face threats in the aerial, cyber and information spaces. Under the MoU, NeGD will act as the Knowledge Partner of CISF.

It will identify academic and technical institutions, Centres of Excellence and expert faculty to design and deliver training built around CISF's operational requirements. NeGD has earlier conducted technology-intensive training programmes with premier institutions, including the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs).

DG CISF Praveer Ranjan, said, "Threats to critical infrastructure today come as much from the sky and from cyberspace as from the ground. Rogue drones, AI-enabled attacks and cyber intrusions into control systems are real concerns for the installations we protect. Through this partnership with NeGD, our personnel will train at the country's leading technical institutions and gain the hands-on skills needed to detect, counter and stay ahead of these threats."

Five Technology Domains: Personnel will be trained in drone operations; anti-drone/counter-unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS) for detecting, tracking and neutralising hostile drones; artificial intelligence and autonomous systems; cyber security for critical infrastructure; and other emerging technologies.

Premier Institutions: Programmes will be delivered in coordination with IITs, DIAT, DRDO laboratories, Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) and other Centres of Excellence. Training will be held on institute campuses, at CISF training establishments or in blended mode.

Certificate to M.Tech Pathways: Options range from short-duration certificate courses and workshops to medium-duration certificate programmes, with *PG Diploma and M.Tech pathways* where approved. *NeGD will bear the approved tuition and course fees*, while CISF will bear the travel, boarding and lodging of its personnel.

CISF-Specific Content: Training will use case studies, standard operating procedures, tabletop exercises and field simulations covering the protection of hydro-power plants, strategic installations, border areas and other high-value assets.

Master Trainers & Review: Trained personnel will serve as master trainers within the Force. A Joint Steering Committee will be set up within 30 days and will meet at least twice a year to review progress and annual training plans.

Nand Kumarum, President & CEO, National e-Governance Division (NeGD), MeitY said, "Technology is reshaping both governance and security. As Knowledge Partner to CISF, NeGD will bring together institutions such as the IITs, DIAT and DRDO laboratories to build practical, mission-focused skills in drones, counter-drone systems, artificial intelligence and cyber security. A technically skilled security force is central to a safe and self-reliant Digital India."
